title: Duvdu
description: A connected marketplace for booking and managing media-production projects from agreement to final delivery.
cardDescription: A marketplace connecting clients and creative service providers through booking, project milestones, asset delivery, and escrow-backed payments.
overview: Duvdu brings clients and creative service providers into one workflow for discovering talent, agreeing on project terms, booking schedules, managing milestones, delivering assets, and releasing payments through escrow.

headings.challenge: Creative projects involve more than finding the right talent.
headings.build: One workflow connecting clients, creators, projects, and payments.
headings.outcome: Duvdu turned a fragmented creative-production process into a connected digital workflow.

problem: Clients and creative professionals were coordinating requirements, schedules, deliverables, contracts, and payments across disconnected channels. That created several points of risk: unclear expectations, missed delivery dates, payment concerns, and limited visibility into the status of a project once work had started. The client wanted Duvdu to provide a structured marketplace where both sides could manage the full project lifecycle in one place.
solution: Oraixen designed and built the platform across web and mobile, supported by a central backend and administration system. Clients can discover service providers, review portfolios, agree on the work, schedule projects, and manage delivery through the platform. Service providers can build their profiles and portfolios, publish previous work, identify collaborators and equipment used, manage bookings, and deliver project assets directly through Duvdu. The platform connects those interactions to project contracts, milestones, deadlines, and an escrow-based payment workflow.
impact: Instead of managing discovery, agreements, scheduling, file delivery, and payments through separate channels, clients and service providers can move through the project lifecycle inside one platform. The escrow workflow also connects payment release to project delivery and client approval, reducing payment risk for both sides.

title: Maqdya
description: A home-services marketplace connecting homeowners with verified craftsmen, contractors, and engineering supervision through one digital platform.
cardDescription: A home-services marketplace connecting homeowners with verified craftsmen, contractors, payments, job tracking, and engineering supervision.
overview: Maqdya brings service discovery, provider portfolios, customer reviews, direct communication, payments, job tracking, and engineering follow-up into one connected experience across web and mobile.

headings.challenge: Finding and managing home-service work required more structure, trust, and visibility.
headings.build: One marketplace connecting homeowners, service providers, payments, and project follow-up.
headings.outcome: Maqdya turned an informal home-services hiring process into a structured digital marketplace.

problem:
Homeowners could find it difficult to evaluate craftsmen and contractors before starting maintenance, finishing, or renovation work.

Service quality, pricing expectations, communication, and project follow-up could vary significantly when the entire process happened through informal offline channels.

For larger renovation and construction work, the client also wanted professional engineering supervision to provide more structured follow-up across project phases.

The goal was to turn an informal hiring process into a marketplace where customers could discover providers, review previous work, communicate, pay, and follow the job through a structured digital workflow.
solution:
Oraixen built Maqdya from the ground up across web, iOS, Android, backend services, APIs, and administration.

Customers can explore service categories, review provider profiles and portfolios, read customer reviews, communicate directly with service providers, and manage service requests through the platform.

Service providers can present their experience and previous work and participate in a structured job workflow rather than relying entirely on informal offline communication.

The system also connects supported electronic payments, order and job tracking, and engineering-supervision workflows for projects that require professional oversight.
impact:
Customers can discover providers, review previous work, communicate, create service requests, complete supported payments, and follow jobs through one connected platform.

Service providers gain a structured digital presence for presenting their work and managing customer opportunities.

For projects that need additional oversight, engineering supervision adds a professional follow-up layer across the work lifecycle.

title: IBDL
description: An enterprise training and certification platform replacing a developer-dependent legacy system with self-service ERP, CRM, and administration workflows.
cardDescription: An enterprise training platform replacing developer-dependent legacy administration with self-service ERP, CRM, certification, staff, and training-center workflows.
overview: IBDL brings training-center operations, trainee records, attendance, certificates, staff administration, CRM activity, course content, and commerce workflows into one enterprise platform.

headings.challenge: Routine business operations depended on developers instead of the administration team.
headings.build: A self-service enterprise platform built around the organization’s real operating workflows.
headings.outcome: IBDL replaced a developer-dependent legacy workflow with a self-service enterprise operating platform.

problem:
The existing platform had become difficult to operate and maintain, with bugs, known security weaknesses, and an administrative interface that did not support routine staff workflows effectively.

Basic operational tasks could require a backend developer to run manual database queries, creating unnecessary dependency on engineering resources for everyday administration.

At the same time, training centers, trainee records, course content, attendance, certificates, employees, CRM activity, and commerce operations needed to be managed through a more connected enterprise system.

The challenge was not simply to redesign the website. It was to replace the legacy operational platform and re-engineer how the organization managed its day-to-day work.
solution:
Oraixen audited the existing system, re-engineered the core business flows, and built a replacement platform spanning the public website, enterprise administration, backend services, APIs, ERP capabilities, CRM workflows, and a new database architecture.

Training-center teams can manage centers, branches, groups, trainees, course materials, attendance, and certificates through the administrative platform.

Internal teams can also manage employees, roles, permissions, and attendance, while CRM and commerce capabilities support public course offerings and related customer and sales activity.

Most importantly, routine administrative operations that previously required direct database intervention can now be performed by authorized staff through the system itself.
impact:
Administrative teams can now manage routine training, trainee, certification, staff, CRM, and commerce operations directly through the platform instead of depending on developers for everyday database intervention.

The rebuild also removed the organization’s reliance on the previous legacy architecture and its known operational and security weaknesses.

The result is a more maintainable operating model where technical teams can focus on engineering while authorized business users manage routine operations through the product itself.

title: Nice One
description: A unified beauty-commerce platform connecting online shopping, multi-channel sales, customer data, and order operations in one system.
cardDescription: A beauty-commerce platform bringing online and supported off-platform orders, customer data, and order tracking into one operational system.
overview: Nice One brings the customer shopping experience and internal sales operations into one connected platform across web, mobile, backend, and administration. Orders from supported off-platform channels can also be captured inside the same operational workflow.

headings.challenge: Sales were happening across channels, but the operation had no single source of truth.
headings.build: One commerce platform for customers, orders, and operational data.
headings.outcome: Nice One brought fragmented sales activity into a more centralized commerce and operations workflow.

problem:
Customer conversations and sales activity were spread across channels such as WhatsApp and other off-platform interactions.

That made it difficult for store teams to keep customer records in one place, create orders consistently, and track sales through a unified workflow.

The business needed more than an online storefront. It needed a connected commerce system that served customers through web and mobile while giving the internal team centralized control over orders and customer data.
solution:
Oraixen contributed to the design and development of the Nice One commerce platform across web, iOS, Android, backend services, APIs, and administration.

Customers can browse the product catalog, add products to their cart, complete checkout, and place orders through the digital storefront.

For store teams, the administration system provides a central place to manage customer records and sales orders.

Orders originating through supported off-platform channels, including WhatsApp-based sales, can also be created manually inside the system so they become part of the same order-management workflow.
impact:
Instead of keeping online orders, supported off-platform sales, and customer information across disconnected channels, the platform gives the business one system for capturing orders, maintaining customer records, and tracking sales activity.

This creates a clearer operational view for store teams while giving customers a structured shopping experience across web and mobile.

title: Sanar
description: A connected healthcare platform for telemedicine and on-demand medical services delivered at home.
cardDescription: A healthcare ecosystem connecting telemedicine, at-home medical services, real-time booking, payments, and insurance workflows.
overview: Sanar connects patients, healthcare providers, administrators, payments, and insurance workflows through one digital ecosystem spanning web and mobile. Patients can book remote consultations and at-home healthcare services based on provider availability and appointment schedules.

headings.challenge: Accessing healthcare at home required a more connected service and booking model.
headings.build: One healthcare ecosystem connecting remote consultations and care delivered at home.
headings.outcome: Sanar turned separate healthcare journeys into one connected digital ecosystem.

problem:
Patients needed a convenient way to access services such as home laboratory tests, nursing visits, physical therapy, child vaccinations, and remote medical consultations without relying on a hospital or clinic visit for every interaction.

The platform also needed to coordinate healthcare-provider availability, appointment scheduling, payments, and insurance coverage through a single digital journey.

The challenge was not simply to build an appointment app. It was to connect patients, healthcare providers, home-care services, telemedicine, administration, payments, and insurance workflows into one operating ecosystem.
solution:
Oraixen contributed to the design and development of Sanar across web, iOS, Android, backend services, APIs, and administration.

Patients can browse available healthcare services, choose appointments based on provider availability, book home-care visits, schedule remote consultations, and complete payments through the platform.

The system also connects healthcare workflows with integrated insurance providers, enabling eligible services to operate within insurance-supported coverage and claim-processing flows.

Administrators manage the platform centrally while healthcare providers participate in scheduled appointments and service delivery.
impact:
Patients can access telemedicine and at-home healthcare services through one platform instead of coordinating appointments, service availability, payments, and insurance through separate channels.

Healthcare providers, administrators, insurance integrations, and patient-facing services operate through the same connected platform architecture.

The ecosystem also supports multiple insurance and corporate partner relationships as part of its operating model.

title: Ghiras Al Usrah
description: A digital counseling platform connecting appointment booking, consultant schedules, payments, and hybrid in-person and video consultations.
cardDescription: A counseling platform replacing paper and Excel workflows with digital booking, consultant scheduling, payments, reminders, and hybrid consultations.
overview: Ghiras Al Usrah replaced a paper and spreadsheet-based consultation workflow with a connected platform across web and mobile. Clients can book consultations and make payments digitally, while consultants manage availability and appointments through a dedicated app.

headings.challenge: Consultations were being managed through paper and spreadsheets instead of one operational system.
headings.build: One platform for booking, scheduling, payments, and hybrid consultations.
headings.outcome: Ghiras Al Usrah replaced a fragmented manual consultation process with one digital operating platform.

problem:
Bookings, consultant schedules, and client appointments depended on manual records and Excel spreadsheets.

That created room for scheduling mistakes, conflicting appointments, and missed sessions when clients or consultants did not receive timely reminders.

The organization also needed to support online payments and virtual consultations without managing those interactions through separate disconnected tools.

The challenge was to turn the full consultation workflow into one digital operating platform.
solution:
Oraixen designed and developed Ghiras Al Usrah across web, mobile applications, backend services, APIs, and administration.

Clients can book supported consultation services, choose available appointments, request express consultations based on consultant availability, make payments through Moyasar, and attend supported virtual sessions through Zoom.

Consultants use a dedicated mobile application to manage schedules, set availability, review appointments, and access virtual consultations.

The administration platform centralizes the operational workflow that had previously depended on paper records and spreadsheets.
impact:
Booking, consultant availability, appointment management, reminders, payments, and supported virtual consultations can now be managed through a connected system instead of paper records and spreadsheets.

This gives clients, consultants, and administrators clearer visibility into appointments and reduces the operational risk created by manual scheduling and missing reminders.

Oraixen designed and developed Delora across the e-commerce website, iOS application, Android application, backend services, APIs, payment integrations, and administration.

Customers can browse a cosmetics-focused catalog, move through categories, search and filter products, add items to their cart, complete checkout, and use supported electronic payment methods.

The customer experience was informed by benchmarking established regional commerce patterns while being designed around Delora’s own cosmetics offering.
impact:
Customers can discover beauty products, shop, complete checkout, and place orders through web, iOS, and Android experiences built around one commerce platform.

At the operational level, store teams can manage products, customers, and orders from one administration environment instead of operating each customer channel independently.

The result is a connected customer and store-management experience designed specifically around Delora’s cosmetics business.
